strengths: Novel information-geometric perspective treating molecules as composite exponential-family distributions on Fisher-Rao manifold, unifying continuous and discrete components geometrically
Clearly identifies and rigorously analyzes trajectory collapse singularities (Section 3.2, Appendix B) when targeting Dirac distributions in both continuous and discrete cases
Principled evolving endpoint strategy that maintains well-defined intermediate distributions while remaining geometrically consistent—elegant solution avoiding ad-hoc regularization
Rigorous mathematical framework including correct e-geodesic derivations, product family closure proof, and equivalence to Fisher Flow Matching with geometric interpretation of SLDM as special case

Exceptional geometric validity: 93.4% PoseBusters passing rate (reference-level), 99.99% bond length accuracy, superior strain energy (8.94/25.96/56.65 quartiles), accurate reproduction of bond/angle/torsion distributions

Comprehensive multi-faceted evaluation: two benchmarks (CrossDock and MolGenBench), multiple metric categories, thorough ablation studies validating each design choice, detailed analysis of molecular properties
Well-structured presentation with clear motivation, intuitive figures, and rigorous appendices balancing accessibility with technical depth
weaknesses: Limited practical applicability: Hit Fraction ~1% for novel targets and 0.01% for out-of-distribution proteins; Hit Recovery=0 for unseen protein families—acknowledged but fundamental gap between 'geometrically plausible' and 'biochemically active' severely limits real-world drug discovery impact

Evolving target schedule (σ₁(t)=0.2(1-t), α₁(t) formulation with λ=0.2) appears ad-hoc with limited justification for specific functional forms; ablations only vary smoothing coefficient not schedule structure; insufficient sensitivity analysis for schedule design choices

Incremental core methodological innovation: implementation follows BFN/PIF's progressive-parameter-refinement paradigm; main novelty is evolving vs. fixed targets which is somewhat evolutionary rather than revolutionary

Missing computational cost analysis: training time (~16 hours) and inference steps (100) mentioned but no wall-clock time comparisons with baselines, no GPU memory analysis, critical for practical adoption assessment

Limited theoretical guarantees: no convergence analysis for evolving endpoint scheme, no approximation error bounds as σ₁(t)→0, loss curve analysis (Fig. 8) demonstrates ill-conditioning but doesn't prove optimality of the evolving solution
Design choice justification lacking: why unitransformer with edge? why 4 layers and 128 hidden dimension? how sensitive to architecture? no architecture ablations provided
Weak statistical rigor: only 100 test proteins with 100 samples each, no confidence intervals or significance testing, no cross-validation details, single best configuration reported

Failure mode analysis absent: no systematic study of when/why method fails; complete failure on out-of-distribution generalization (Hit Recovery=0) not investigated; no discussion of challenging protein families or molecule classes
Reproducibility concerns: no code release mentioned, some hyperparameters empirically selected (smoothing coefficient), multiple interdependent components, schedule selection procedure unclear

strengths: Novel information-geometric framework using exponential geodesics on Fisher-Rao manifolds, grounded in rigorous mathematics with proper treatment of singularities in Dirac targets

Elegant solution via dynamic endpoints that maintains well-conditioned distributions throughout training while progressing toward target—automatically calibrates loss weights across modalities via Fisher-Rao metric

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple benchmarks (CrossDock, MolGenBench) with extensive ablations (Table 4) demonstrating necessity of each component; naive EGF baseline shows 64% vs 93.4% PB-Valid

Superior geometric validity: 93.4% PoseBusters passing rate with exceptional bond length/angle distributions (JSD=0.031-0.034) and low strain energy; Figures 9-11 show close alignment with reference distributions

Synchronized multi-modal learning demonstrated through intermediate state analysis: achieves 96% molecular validity at t=0.3 vs 29% for TargetDiff, showing earlier emergence of chemically meaningful prototypes

Well-written with clear motivation, effective visual explanations, rigorous mathematical development, comprehensive appendices (proofs, loss derivations, algorithms), and honest treatment of limitations
Strong theoretical contribution with generalizability beyond SBDD; connection to SLDM (Appendix E) provides geometric interpretation of recent efficient methods
weaknesses: Severe gap between geometric improvements and real-world drug discovery: Hit Fraction <1% on MolGenBench across all methods (Table 2-3); Hit Recovery=0 for unseen targets. Paper acknowledges but doesn't bridge this fundamental limitation
Baseline comparison inconsistency: slight underperformance vs MolPilot on primary metric (PB-Valid) is deferred to Appendix F and should be clarified in main text if true

Smoothing coefficient λ=0.2 presented as hyperparameter with limited theoretical justification; while ablation shows optimality around 0.2, principled choice or functional form (why λ(1-t) vs alternatives?) lacks theoretical grounding

Natural-parameter space formulation feels somewhat disconnected from practical sampling: connection between Eq. 9 (parameter velocity) and Algorithm 2 (actual sampling) could be more explicit; sample-space characterization relegated to appendix

Method complexity (evolving schedules, Dirichlet parameterization, smoothing coefficients, bond diffusion) with multiple hyperparameters but limited guidance for practitioners; adoption barriers not discussed
Computational efficiency not improved: 16h training (A100), 1.5 mol/s inference comparable to baselines—no speed advantage despite theoretical sophistication
Limited ablation on functional form choices: why σ̃₁(t)=λ(1-t) specifically? Appendix shows λ range (0.1-0.4) but not robustness to functional form alternatives
